subject.title: [Feature]: Add $EDITOR compose mode in TUI (external editor handoff) for multiline prompts

question: Should OpenClaw add a core TUI external-editor compose flow now, and which trigger plus local editor/tempfile safety contract should it use?
rationale: The implementation surface is clear, but launching VISUAL/EDITOR and writing prompt drafts to disk is both a product UX choice and a local security boundary that automation should not decide alone.

options.title: Approve Guarded Core Flow
options.body: Implement the external-editor handoff in core TUI with an approved key or slash trigger, argv-safe process launch, restrictive temp-file handling, cleanup, no auto-submit, tests, and docs.

options.title: Hold For UX And Security Spec
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers choose the trigger model and write the local editor/tempfile safety contract.

options.title: Prefer Inline Composer Improvements
options.body: Decline or narrow this request if maintainers want long-prompt work handled through inline multiline editing, vi mode, or composer expansion instead of local process handoff.

recommendation.title: Approve Guarded Core Flow
recommendation.body: Implement the external-editor handoff in core TUI with an approved key or slash trigger, argv-safe process launch, restrictive temp-file handling, cleanup, no auto-submit, tests, and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: He has already reviewed this exact issue and is the strongest current routing signal for the TUI command, composer, docs, and security-boundary decision.
